claim: The Bund is a free 24-hour public waterfront promenade where sunset-to-blue-hour is the strongest photo window; walk north from East Nanjing Road Station (Line 2/10, Exit 2) toward Waibaidu Bridge for layered facade-and-skyline shots, pairing it with East Nanjing Road in one evening route.
quote: sunset to blue hour is the strongest window for photos ... free public waterfront promenade ... East Nanjing Road Station (Line 2/10, Exit 2) — best entry point ... pairing The Bund with East Nanjing Road in one continuous evening route

claim: Shanghai Tower's 118th-floor observation deck (Top of Shanghai Observatory) is open 08:30-21:30 with adult tickets normally RMB 180.
quote: Shanghai Tower 118th Floor Observation Deck is open from 08:30-21:30 ... the normal entry price for adults is ¥180, with holiday prices at ¥199

claim: Yu Garden opens 09:00-16:30 (ticketing stops 16:00), closed Mondays except National Day, admission RMB 40 (Apr-Jun, Sep-Nov) or RMB 30 (Jul-Aug, Dec-Mar); the adjacent Yuyuan Bazaar and the night-lit Nine Bend Bridge are free.
quote: 09:00 - 16:30 (Ticketing stops at 16:00); Closed on Mondays ... April-June & Sept-Nov | 40 ... July-Aug & Dec-March | 30 ... Nine Bend Bridge offers free nighttime viewing with colorful lighting outside paid garden areas

claim: The Oriental Pearl Tower is open daily 09:00-21:00 (last entry 20:30); the Double Sphere ticket is RMB 199 and the Triple Sphere (top deck) RMB 299, with evening visits and 7:30/8:30/9:30 PM light shows recommended.
quote: daily from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM, with last entry at 8:30 PM ... Double Sphere Ticket: ¥199 ... Triple Sphere Ticket: ¥299 ... scheduled light shows at 7:30 PM, 8:30 PM, and 9:30 PM

claim: Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street is a free pedestrian-only zone running ~1200m from People's Square to the Bund, lined with department stores and time-honored shops, most lively at night.
quote: The pedestrian section is about 1200 meters long, stretching from People's Square in the west to the Bund in the east ... Nanjing Road is most lively and charming at night.

claim: Best times for Nanjing Road are weekday mornings (10am-12pm) or after 8pm for the lights, avoiding weekends, lunch (12-2pm) and dinner rush (6-8pm); People's Square (Line 1/2/8) anchors its western end.
quote: Best time to visit is weekday mornings (10am-12pm) or after 8pm for lights. Avoid weekends, holidays, lunch hours (12-2pm), dinner rush (6-8pm)

claim: The Former French Concession is defined by plane-tree-lined avenues with 1920s Art Deco mansions beside third-wave coffee roasters; best walked weekday mornings 9-11:30am, 3-4 hours.
quote: leafy, plane-tree-lined avenues where 1920s Art Deco mansions sit next to third-wave coffee roasters

claim: Key FFC streets for walking include Wukang Lu, Fuxing Lu, Anfu Lu, Wulumuqi Lu, Yongfu Lu, Xinle Lu and Changle Lu, packed with hip cafes, concept bars, boutiques, galleries and antiques stores.
quote: huge variety of hip cafes and restaurants, concept bars and breweries, boutiques, art galleries and antiques stores. Wukang Lu is a beautiful street, quaint and pretty, with outdoor cafes

claim: The Wukang Road-Anfu Road walk is about 2.5 km and 3-4 hours, reached via Metro Line 10/11 to Jiao Tong University Station exit 7; a hangout for young locals and fashion crowds.
quote: The route is about 2.5 km and takes 3-4 hours including stops for cafes and photo spots. By Metro: Line 10 or 11 to Jiao Tong University Station, exit 7.

claim: Wukang Mansion, designed by Hungarian architect Laszlo Hudec in 1924, is a triangular French Renaissance/Art Deco building at a road junction and Shanghai's top photo-icon landmark.
quote: Designed by Hungarian architect Laszlo Hudec in 1924, Wukang Mansion stands as one of Shanghai's most iconic landmarks. The most distinctive feature of Wukang Mansion is its triangular shape

claim: Xintiandi is fully commercialized restored shikumen with no residents, offering designer stores and upscale dining; Tianzifang keeps residents living above shops in a maze of art-studio alleys.
quote: Xintiandi is totally commercialized without any local residents living in these shikumen buildings... In Tianzifang, people still live on the floor over the restaurants and shops

claim: Xintiandi (completed 2001) preserved shikumen exterior facades, stone gateways and lane layouts while rebuilding interiors as upscale commercial space; shikumen means 'stone warehouse gate'.
quote: shikumen literally means stone warehouse gate, describing the buildings' vaulted stone doorways

claim: The Jing'an area centers on the thousand-year-old Jing'an Temple and Nanjing West Road, pairing luxury malls (Plaza 66, Jing'an Kerry Centre, Jiuguang) with plane-tree lanes, boutiques and Jing'an Park.
quote: revolving around the thousand-year-old Jing'an Temple and stretching out to iconic streets like Nanjing West Road, Yuyuan Road, and Julu Road

claim: Jing'an Temple charges roughly 50 RMB; its Mahavira Hall holds a large bronze Buddha and a jade Buddha, and visitors should wear modest clothing.
quote: For 50 RMB visitors can view the three main halls and their assorted historical relics, including an enormous Jade Buddha

claim: Shanghai's Old City around Yu Garden offers traditional buildings, street food and small shops in a lively pedestrian-friendly bazaar, dramatically lit with red lanterns at night.
quote: Beautiful traditional buildings, the smell of street food and many small shops create a magical and lively place

claim: Xintiandi houses the Shikumen Open House Museum (118 Alley, Taicang Road) recreating a 1920s-30s shikumen home and the free First Communist Congress Museum.
quote: Visit the Shikumen Open House Museum (No.25, 118 Alley, Taicang Road), set up like a traditional shikumen-style home from the 1920s and 1930s

claim: Shanghai Museum East in Pudong is free for individual visitors with valid ID, open Wednesday to Monday 10:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00), closed Tuesdays, at 1952 Century Avenue.
quote: Wednesday to Monday, 10:00-18:00 (last entry at 17:00)... Free entry for individual visitors with a valid ID through the B1 East Gate... 1952 Century Avenue, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

claim: Shanghai Museum on People's Square is free, open 9:00-17:00 (last entry 16:00), closed Mondays, at 201 Renmin Avenue, Huangpu.
quote: 9:00~17:00 with latest entry at 16:00, closed on Mondays except national holidays... No. 201 Ren Min Da Dao, Huangpu District, Shanghai... Reservation for individual visitors is not required.

claim: The People's Square branch closes May 6 to end of June 2026 to install new exhibitions, with an ancient Americas civilizations show (1,000+ relics, Olmec/Maya/Aztec/Inca) and a July 2026 calligraphy/painting show following.
quote: temporarily close from May 6th to the end of June 2026... exhibition On Top of the World Tree: Ancient Civilizations of the Americas... over 1,000 exquisite cultural relics from the Americas... Olmec, Maya, Aztec, and Inca.

claim: Power Station of Art, China's first state-run contemporary art museum in a former power plant, opens 11:00-19:00 (last entry 18:00), closed Mondays; permanent collection free, special exhibitions around 60 RMB.
quote: opening hours are 11:00 AM - 7:00 PM (last entry at 6:00 PM, closed on Mondays)... tickets are 60 RMB per person... children between 6 to 18 years old and seniors between 60 to 70 years old enjoy a 50% discount.

claim: Long Museum West Bund charges CNY 50-100 depending on exhibition, free the first Tuesday of each month, open Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00 (summer) closed Mondays.
quote: CNY 50/100 (Depending on the exhibitions)... complimentary entry on the first Tuesday of each month... April 1 - October 31: Tuesday-Sunday, 10:00-18:00 (tickets stop selling at 17:00)... Closed Mondays.

claim: Long Museum West Bund, designed by Liu Yichun, is known for its umbrella-arch fair-faced concrete architecture, with contemporary art on upper floors and ancient Chinese art in a basement white-box gallery.
quote: distinctive umbrella arch structure designed by architect Liu Yichun... overhanging arched space surface is poured with fine-grained fair-faced concrete... basement houses permanent exhibition space for ancient Chinese art treasures.

claim: Centre Pompidou x West Bund Museum, a France-China partnership inaugurated 2019 and renewed in 2024 for five more years, charges 40-80 RMB, opens Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30), closed Mondays.
quote: Tickets are 40-80 RMB, varying by exhibition... Tuesday to Sunday, 11:00 AM to 6:00 PM (last entry 5:30 PM), closed on Mondays... In 2024, the partnership was renewed for another five years.

claim: The Centre Pompidou x West Bund semi-permanent tour 'Reinventing Landscape' runs April 28 2025 to October 18 2026, exploring the transformation of landscape art across the 20th-21st centuries.
quote: the fourth semi-permanent tour, Reinventing Landscape, runs from April 28, 2025, to October 18, 2026, highlighting the art of landscape and the profound transformations it has undergone over the 20th and 21st centuries.

claim: M50 Creative Park at 50 Moganshan Road, a former textile mill turned art cluster, holds 140+ studios and galleries (including ShanghART) with free entry, open daily roughly 8:00-22:00.
quote: M50 is home to over 140 studios and galleries... ShanghART Gallery, one of the most influential galleries in contemporary China... open daily 8:00 AM-10:00 PM with free entry; some galleries may charge extra fees.

claim: Shanghai Tower's 118th-floor observation deck (world's second-tallest building) lists adult entry around 180 RMB, open 08:30-21:30.
quote: the normal entry price for adults is ¥180... Shanghai Tower 118th Floor Observation Deck is open from 08:30-21:30.

claim: Jade Buddha Temple at 170 Anyuan Road, Putuo, opens daily 8:00-16:30; entry is free with a 10 RMB charge to enter the Jade Buddha Hall.
quote: open daily from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM... admission is free, but an additional 10 RMB is required to visit the Jade Buddha Hall, with no reservation needed... 170 Anyuan Road, Putuo District, Shanghai.

claim: ERA acrobatics show at Shanghai Circus World sells tickets across five seating categories roughly 580-800+ RMB, a long-running high-tech acrobatic spectacle.
quote: ticket prices range from RMB 580 to RMB 800+, depending on seating category... There are five seating categories available, with an upgrade option for prime positions.

claim: Jia Jia Tang Bao is a family-run xiaolongbao legend since 1986 near People's Square with Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition, thin wrappers with 18 folds and a signature pork-crab basket around 39 RMB, known for long queues.
quote: Jia Jia Tang Bao stands out as one of Shanghai's most famous xiaolongbao restaurants, a family-run legend since 1986 that's earned Michelin Bib Gourmand nods... pork-crab filling at just 39 RMB (USD$5.50) per basket.

claim: Din Tai Fung is a Taipei-origin chain (not Shanghainese) that is the most reliable, spotless, English-friendly option for first-time xiaolongbao eaters but pricier than local spots, with a popular truffle xiaolongbao.
quote: A global brand originating from Taipei, so it's not actually Shanghainese, but still one of the most reliable places for xiaolongbao in Shanghai... The truffle xiaolongbao is a must-try here.

claim: Yang's Dumpling (Xiao Yang Sheng Jian) is a Shanghai shengjianbao chain founded 1994 serving pan-fried pork soup buns at roughly 13 RMB for four.
quote: Yang's Dumpling sheng jian bao costs ¥13 for 4 buns... a Shanghainese Chinese dish that was formed in Shanghai in 1994 by Mrs. Yang.

claim: Shanghai's classic local breakfast is the 'Four Warriors' (si da jin gang): da bing sesame flatbread, you tiao fried dough sticks, ci fan glutinous rice rolls, and dou jiang soy milk (sweet or savory).
quote: The Four Warriors (si da jin gang) refer to four... glutinous rice rolls (ci fan), soy milk (dou jiang), fried crullers (you tiao), and sesame pancake (da bing).

claim: Shanghai's 2026 Michelin Bib Gourmand list features affordable local spots including noodle houses (A Niang Mian Guan, Rongjia Noodle Soup with Yellow Croaker, Jingmei Wuxi Noodle) and Nanxiang Steamed Bun at City God Temple for xiaolongbao.
quote: Nanxiang Steamed Bun at the City God Temple location maintains its recognition for traditional xiaolongbao... Rongjia Noodle Soup with Yellow Croaker (Jing'an) features fish-based broths

claim: Two emblematic Shanghainese benbang dishes are scallion oil noodles (congyou banmian) and sweet caramel-glazed braised pork belly (hongshao rou), the latter stewed at least 90 minutes.
quote: Scallion Oil Noodles, Congyou Banmian... Braised Pork Belly, or Hong Shao Rou... Shanghai people prefer sweet flavors. Thus, the seasonings of Shanghai-style Braised Pork Belly feature caramel sugar

claim: Hairy crab season runs roughly October-November (females best late Sept-Oct for roe, males late Oct-Nov for meat); during season crabs appear everywhere from restaurants to subway vending machines.
quote: October and November is when Shanghai hairy crabs are in season... females are known for their fragrant roe with peak season from late September to October, while males have firmer meat... late October to November.

claim: Notable hairy crab specialists include Wang Bao He (near the Bund, established 1744), Michelin-starred Cheng Long Hang Crab Palace on Jiujiang Lu, and Cejerdary famed for hairy crab noodles at The Bund.
quote: Cheng Long Hang Crab Palace... Jiujiang Lu location in Huangpu holding a Michelin one-star. Wang Bao He is a specialty restaurant for hairy crab in Shanghai, located near the Bund and established in 1744

claim: Shanghai's classic snack/food streets include Huanghe Road (near People's Square, benbang restaurants and Jiajia soup dumplings), Yunnan Road (time-honored brands like Abao fried pork chop, Xiandelai rice cake), and Wujiang Road (Yang's buns, Nanxiang buns, wonton).
quote: Huanghe Road... home to many time-honored restaurants offering Shanghai local Benbang Cuisine... Yunnan Road... Abao Fried Pork Chop, Xiaojinling Salted Duck, Xiandelai Chop Rice Cake... Wujiang Road... Yang's Fried Stuffed Bun, Nanxiang Steamed Stuffed Bun

claim: Shanghai is the world's densest coffee market with 10,336 cafes as of early 2026, with specialty independents concentrated in the Former French Concession and showcasing single-origin Yunnan-grown Chinese beans.
quote: Shanghai has officially solidified its position as the world's most dense and innovative coffee market, boasting 10,336 cafes—outperforming New York, London, and Tokyo combined.

claim: Huxinting Teahouse, reached by a zigzag bridge inside Yu Garden, is Shanghai's oldest commercial teahouse (over 240 years, teahouse since 1855), recently renovated in 2026 with affordable morning tea on the first floor.
quote: Huxinting Teahouse is known as the 'First Teahouse of Shanghai'... converted into a teahouse in 1855... newly renovated teahouse... the first floor retaining affordable morning tea service

claim: FLAIR on the 58th floor of The Ritz-Carlton Shanghai Pudong is widely rated Shanghai's best rooftop bar, facing the Oriental Pearl Tower with a panorama of the Bund and Huangpu River; Bar Rouge has closed and reopened as the KEV nightclub.
quote: FLAIR, The Ritz-Carlton Shanghai, Pudong ... 58th floor ... Oriental Pearl Tower and the rare panorama of the Bund and meandering Huangpu River ... Notable Closures: Bar Rouge (now KEV nightclub)

claim: The Rooftop Guide names FLAIR, The Roof at The Shanghai EDITION, and Highline as Shanghai's top three rooftop bars, with FLAIR cocktails starting around 175 RMB, and lists Bar Rouge, Vue Bar, M on the Bund and Kartel as permanently closed.
quote: The top 3 Shanghai rooftop destinations are FLAIR, The Roof at The Shanghai EDITION, and Highline ... Cocktails start around 175 RMB ... Bar Rouge, Vue Bar, M on the Bund, Kartel have permanently closed

claim: FLAIR Rooftop Restaurant & Bar is the official venue at the Ritz-Carlton Pudong, billed as one of the highest rooftop bars in the world with skyline views, and runs a seasonal terrace opening party.
quote: Flair Rooftop Restaurant & Bar ... 2026 terrace opening party | skyline reawaken

claim: Speak Low is a hidden speakeasy entered behind a bar-tools shop that has placed on the World's 50 Best Bars list every year since 2016, peaking at #10 globally in 2017, with classic cocktails downstairs and rare spirits and private rooms upstairs.
quote: Speak Low still maintains its position in the upper echelons of both The World's and Asia's 50 Best Bars lists

claim: Sober Company is a multi-concept venue (Sober Cafe, Sober Kitchen, Sober Society) from the Speak Low team, with the creative Chinese-ingredient cocktails at Sober Society, and is a regular on Asia's 50 Best Bars.
quote: a constant among Asia's 50 Best Bars in recent years, Sober Company is a venue in three parts ... Sober Society, with its focus on Chinese ingredients, is where the creative cocktails are at

claim: Union Trading Company pairs chef Austin Hu's food with cocktail champion Yao Lu's drinks as a neighbourhood bar and Asia's 50 Best entry, with a signature Shanghai Breakfast cocktail.
quote: Chef Austin Hu takes care of the food and cocktail champion Yao Lu looks after the libations ... one of Asia's 50 Best Bars. A recent #97 spot on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025

claim: Huangpu River night cruises run roughly 50 minutes past the Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower and Shanghai Tower, with the best time after 7pm; peak-season (Feb 26-Nov 25) night tickets cost about 135 RMB and off-season about 115 RMB.
quote: night cruises cost ¥135, while off-season pricing (November 26-February 25) is ¥115 ... The most popular cruise option is the 50-minute classic cruise

claim: The Bund and Pudong building facades are illuminated each evening roughly 6pm-10pm, making a post-7pm Huangpu River cruise the prime way to see the lit skyline.
quote: The Bund's lights are typically illuminated from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM ... The best time for a cruise is after 7:00 PM

claim: The Jazz Bar at the Fairmont Peace Hotel on the Bund hosts the Old Jazz Band (Guinness record as world's oldest, average age ~82) playing nightly about 7pm-11:30pm, with entry around 418 RMB applied as a food-and-drink minimum spend.
quote: the Old Jazz Band ... holds the Guinness World Record for "The World's Oldest Jazz Band." The band ... plays every evening from 7pm to 11:30pm ... Entry is ¥418 per person, which may be used for food and drink

claim: JZ Club at 46 Fuxing Xi Lu in the French Concession is where locals go for jazz, showcasing homegrown and international talent across styles from orchestral to avant-garde, offering a livelier alternative to the Peace Hotel's nostalgic act.
quote: JZ jazz Club is nestled on Fuxing Lu in the leafy streets of the French Concession, and is where Shanghai residents go to hear their jazz ... jazz of almost every conceivable style, from orchestral to avant garde

claim: China's upgraded 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit applies to citizens of 55 countries who hold onward interline tickets to a third country and enter via any of 60 open ports including Shanghai.
quote: Citizens of 55 countries... may stay in designated areas for up to 10 days... must hold valid international travel documents and interline tickets with confirmed dates and seats to a third country or region... 60 open ports across 24 provinces... such as Beijing and Shanghai

claim: Eligible 240-hour transit nationalities include the US, Canada, UK, Australia, all EU/Schengen states, Japan, South Korea and Singapore; visitors may do tourism, business or family visits but not work or study.
quote: China Visa-Free Travel 2026: 77 Countries & 240-Hour Transit

claim: Since late 2023 foreigners can link a Visa/Mastercard directly inside Alipay (Me > Bank Cards) with passport verification, no Chinese bank account or local SIM needed, and it works at most merchants in 2026.
quote: Alipay allows foreigners to link Visa/Mastercard directly without needing a TourCard or Chinese bank account by downloading Alipay, going to Me > Bank Cards, adding your card, and completing passport verification, and it works at most merchants now

claim: The practical 2026 strategy is to set up both Alipay and WeChat Pay (when one fails at a merchant the other often works), backed by some cash and a physical card for hotels, since QR payments are near-universal while foreign cards remain hit-or-miss locally.
quote: set up both apps, as when one wallet fails at a specific merchant, the other often works... Alipay or WeChat Pay in China, backed up by a little cash (RMB) and a physical card for hotels

claim: Zhujiajiao is the easiest water town from Shanghai: Metro Line 17 from Hongqiao Railway Station reaches Zhujiajiao Station in about 1 hour (trains every ~10 min); the town has no entrance fee but a through-ticket for 8 attractions costs 60 RMB (80 RMB with boat ride).
quote: Metro Line 17 is the only metro line running from Shanghai City to Zhujiajiao... taking about 1 hour... A through ticket of 8 attractions is 60 yuan, and a through ticket of 8 attractions including boat sightseeing is 80 yuan

claim: Zhujiajiao charges no town entrance ticket and a taxi from downtown Shanghai takes about an hour costing roughly 150-200 RMB; Bus 1510 runs from Zhujiajiao metro station directly into the town.
quote: take Bus No. 1510, the tourist bus directly to Zhujiajiao Water Town

claim: The Shanghai Maglev runs Pudong Airport to Longyang Road metro (Line 2) in about 7-8 minutes at up to 300 km/h; a single trip is 50 CNY, discounted to 40 CNY with a same-day boarding pass, operating 6:45am-9:52pm.
quote: A single trip is 50 CNY, but if you show a same-day flight ticket (boarding pass)... it is discounted to 40 CNY... covers the 30km trip in 7 minutes and 20 seconds to 8 minutes... 6:45 AM–9:52 PM

claim: For the Shanghai metro, foreigners can pay by scanning a QR code with Alipay/WeChat at the gate or buy a rechargeable Shanghai Public Transportation (Jiaotong) Card at any station or convenience store.
quote: the easiest and most popular payment method is using a Shanghai Public Transportation Card (also known as the Jiaotong Card)... Another option is using mobile payment apps like Alipay or WeChat Pay by scanning a QR code at the entry gate

claim: DiDi ride-hailing offers a full English interface with real-time driver-chat translation, can be run as a WeChat mini-program with no separate app, accepts foreign Visa/Mastercard, and needs no Chinese phone number.
quote: the interface is in English, and driver messages come through auto-translated both ways... Didi accepts Visa, Mastercard, and other major international cards... You don't need a Chinese phone number

claim: Suzhou is a fast longer day trip: over 450 high-speed train pairs run daily from Shanghai (mostly Hongqiao), taking ~21-45 minutes with second-class fares of CNY 21-52.
quote: the shortest travel time of 15 minutes... a second class seat costs from CNY 21 (US$ 3)... second-class seats on G trains cost CNY 21 - 52

claim: June in Shanghai averages 27C high / 20C low with 159mm rain over ~15 rainy days and 79% humidity (the year's highest), as the city enters its plum rain season around mid-June.
quote: Average High: 27°C... Average Low: 20°C... Rainfall: 159mm... Rainy Days: 15 days... Humidity: 79%... around mid-June each year, Shanghai enters the plum rainy season

claim: The best times to visit Shanghai are spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October), which are mild, drier and less crowded, whereas summer is hottest, rainiest and most typhoon-prone.
quote: The best times to visit Shanghai are during the spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) months... Summer (June to August) is Shanghai's hottest, rainiest, and most typhoon-prone season
